title: wg: land catch-up as tiers, PR first and draft last (how much can be SHOULD/MAY)
description:
Mark asked (2026-11-26) how much of his drafts could be SHOULDs and MAYs
in the EXISTING drafts instead of new documents. For catch-up the answer
splits cleanly into three tiers, and the tiering is better tactics than
proposing the whole draft at once (bead mimid-1wgh.37.14).

## The insertion point already exists

protocol-07 §5.5 "Fanout Messages and Room Events" already says:

  If the hub server does not contain an HTTP 201 response code, then it
  SHOULD retry the request, respecting any guidance provided by the
  server in HTTP header fields such as Retry-After.

So the document already discusses retry. What it does not say is what
happens when a hub STOPS retrying, which is where the message is lost
and nobody is told. Tier 1 is a few sentences in a paragraph that is
already about this.

## Tier 1: SHOULD/MAY text in protocol-07 §5.5, no new wire at all

1. A hub MUST (or SHOULD, if the WG prefers) fan each accepted event out
   to every provider with a participant in the room at acceptance. This
   is probably already the intent, so it is a clarification -- but it is
   also the prerequisite for any sequence to be contiguous per
   destination, so getting it stated is worth doing first and cheaply.
2. A hub SHOULD state the window for which it retains a room's fanout,
   so a follower can know what it could ever recover.
3. A follower that knows it is missing part of a room's history MUST NOT
   present that room to its users as complete. No new bytes: a
   prohibition on lying.
4. NEW IDEA, not in draft-atwood-mimi-catchup: a hub that abandons a
   delivery SHOULD make that fact available to the follower.

   Point 4 is worth its own thought. The whole draft is follower-side
   detection, but the party that KNOWS a delivery was lost is the hub --
   it is the one that gave up. A hub could keep a per (room, follower)
   "deliveries abandoned" marker and surface it on next contact. That is
   far cheaper than retaining the fanout itself, and it buys the honesty
   requirement with no sequence numbering and no catchUp endpoint.
   It buys detection and NOT recovery, which may be the right trade for
   an implementation that does not want catch-up at all.

## Tier 2: one small addition, most of the value

The sequence header alone, as a MAY in §5.5:

  A hub MAY include a mimi-fanout-sequence header field in a /notify
  request. If it does, the value MUST be per-room, begin at 1, and
  increase by exactly one per fanout of that room, and MUST NOT be
  reused or renumbered.

That alone lets a follower DETECT a gap, with no new endpoint, no
retention obligation and no catch-up. Detection without recovery is
still an enormous improvement over silence, because it is what makes
tier 1 point 3 implementable rather than vacuous.

## Tier 3: needs the draft

catchUp itself -- the operation, CatchUpRequest, CatchUpResponse and its
response codes, and the directory member. Recovery needs a new
operation; nothing softer gets it. This is what
draft-atwood-mimi-catchup should narrow to if tiers 1 and 2 land
separately.

## The tactic

Propose tier 1 as a PR or issue against protocol-07: small, mostly
clarifying, and it puts the PROBLEM in the WG's own document. Then tier
2 as a second small one. Then the draft, which by that point defines
only the mechanism and can cite the document's own text for why it is
needed.

Each step is independently useful, and a WG that says no to the draft
can still have said yes to the honesty requirement, which is the part
that actually matters.

## Not assessed

The same lens should be run over draft-atwood-mimi-provider-auth and
draft-atwood-mimi-calls: which of their requirements need new bytes and
which are guidance that could be SHOULD/MAY text in protocol-07 or
mimi-content. Neither has been read for this; judging them needs that
first.

Nothing upstream without Mark's OK (memory: dont-flood-upstream), and no
JMAP in any of it (AGENTS.md).
